units.note: 1 Blender unit == 1 m. No arbitrary scaling anywhere.

world.origin_note: Base sits on the world origin; the map extends north.

thermal_disclaimer: Blender performs no radiometric simulation. These are apparent surface temperatures for a temperate late-afternoon condition, intended to be transcribed into Gazebo thermal camera / <temperature> parameters. Walls, rubble and snowpack are opaque in LWIR: objects flagged opaque_to_thermal must occlude. Ambient air temperature per lighting preset is in lighting_presets[*].ambient_c; contrast is human_surface_temp minus local background, not an absolute.

DAY.note: Reference condition. RGB easy, thermal contrast modest.

CLOUDY.note: Flat light, weak shadows, low texture contrast.

SUNSET.note: Long shadows, strong glare, worst case for RGB exposure. Terrain still holds residual heat.

LOW_LIGHT.note: Civil twilight. RGB degrading, thermal improving.

NIGHT.note: Base floodlights on, everything else near-dark. Human-to-background delta T is largest here: this is where thermal earns its place. Not pitch black -- the point is fusion, not sensor failure.

FOG.note: Visual range ~35 m. LiDAR degrades with the model you choose in Gazebo; Blender volumetrics do not export.

RAIN.note: Wet surfaces: drop friction_mu by ~0.15 on ROAD/CONCRETE and by ~0.08 elsewhere in the Gazebo surface params.

DUST.note: Desert sector only. Sand-laden air: RGB washes out, LiDAR returns get noisy.

SNOWFALL.note: Whiteout-like. Do NOT model this as total sensor failure; the objective is robust navigation, not a scripted blackout.

weather_disclaimer: Fog / rain / dust / snowfall are Blender-side visual variations plus this table. Gazebo needs its own <scene><fog> and sensor noise configuration -- none of it crosses the mesh export.

buildings.label: 3-storey office block. West face of the urban canyon.
3-storey block. East face of the urban canyon; ~7.5 m of open street between 001 and 002 with 10 m walls either side -> GPS multipath / sky occlusion, and wide enough to drive.
Partially collapsed 2-storey. Victim inside, visible ONLY through the collapsed north-east wall opening.
Warehouse. Wide roller entrance + narrow side door + one blocked door; dark interior, rooms and a corridor.
Collapsed house. One survivable void with a crawl-height opening; casualty adjacent, NOT buried.
Partially collapsed 2-storey. Three approaches: wide (unsafe), narrow (tight clearance), blocked. Forces entrance selection.

vehicles.label: Abandoned car, engine still warm. Casualty PERSON_015 alongside -> warm vehicle vs warm human discrimination.
Crushed car under debris, parked at the Street D kerb -- an obstacle beside the carriageway, not across it
Overturned truck blocking Urban Street C -> forces a reroute
Stranded vehicle at the flood margin, partly in the channel

prop_clusters.note: Staging yard on the apron. First movable things the robot sees, on flat ground where a failed push is unambiguous.
Cones narrowing the base gate. Directly on the exit path -- the robot meets these in the first ten metres of every run.
Street furniture strewn across Urban Street A, the alternative when Street C is blocked by the overturned truck.
Inside the 7.5 m canyon between URB_001 and URB_002. Narrows an already tight corridor, and the walls leave nowhere to swing wide -- the robot either pushes through or backs out.
Loading yard outside the warehouse roller door.
Loose pipe and sheet at the collapse-field margin, beside the rubble bypass. Rolling pipe on sloped debris is the nastiest case here: it moves after the robot has passed it.
Debris washed onto the flood plain. Scattered, low contrast against mud.
Dropped stores beside the desert track. Sand gives low friction under both the prop and the robot.
Forward staging point on the forest track, under canopy shadow.

BARREL.note: Part-full steel drum. Tips, then rolls.

CRATE.note: Supply crate. Slides and tumbles, does not roll.

PALLET.note: Flat and low -- a genuine LiDAR ambiguity: the robot must decide whether to drive over it.

CONE.note: Traffic cone. Light enough to knock flat without stopping the robot -- tests whether contact is detected at all.

PANEL.note: Loose sheet metal. Low friction, slides a long way.

PIPE.note: Loose pipe lying across the ground. Rolls perpendicular to its axis and not at all along it.

JERRYCAN.note: Fuel can. Small enough to vanish under a bumper.

BIN.note: Wheeled bin. Tall, light, topples easily.

dynamic_obstacles.note: Two mechanisms, deliberately different. Humans and carried loads follow scripted trajectories and move whatever the robot does. Props have mass and inertia and no script at all -- they move only when something pushes them, which is the case that punishes a planner for assuming a static world and for assuming 'it moved once' means 'it will keep moving'.
